page_title: Implementing precise interrupts in pipelined processors

sources.entry: Implementing Precise Interrupts in Pipelined Processors - Introduces the reorder buffer and defines a precise exception as in-order commit of out-of-order results.

summary.title: Implementing precise interrupts in pipelined processors
summary.one_liner: Learn five ways to make interrupts precise in pipelined CPUs, where saved state matches sequential execution even when instructions finish out of order.
takeaways: An interrupt is precise when the saved state matches a sequential model where each instruction completes before the next begins.
Forcing instructions to complete in architectural order is the simplest solution but costs at least 16% performance on the Cray-1S simulation.
The other four solutions let instructions finish out of order and add hardware to restore a precise state on interrupt.
Three of the out-of-order solutions lose as little as 3% performance, per the paper's simulation results.
The paper briefly discusses extensions to vector architectures, virtual memory, and linear pipelines.
summary.summary: This is a research paper on the precise interrupt problem in pipelined processors, where an instruction may start before its predecessors finish. It describes and evaluates five solutions. The first enforces in-order completion and state update, while the other four allow out-of-order completion and add hardware, such as a reorder buffer, to restore precise state. The methods are discussed in a parallel pipeline context and evaluated with simulation results for the Cray-1S scalar architecture. The page text is only the abstract, so details of the individual hardware designs are not visible here.
